top_stories.title: Cisco Zero-Day Highlights API Endpoint Authentication Issues
top_stories.summary: A maximum-severity authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-76460) has been discovered in Cisco's Identity Services Engine (ISE), receiving a CVSS score of 10 out of 10. The zero-day flaw affects API endpoint authentication in Cisco ISE, a widely used network access control and identity management platform.

top_stories.title: Cisco Warns of New Zero-Day ISE Auth Bypass (CVSS 10.0) Exploited in Active Attacks
top_stories.summary: Cisco has disclosed a maximum-severity (CVSS 10.0) zero-day vulnerability in its Identity Services Engine (ISE), tracked as CVE-2026-76460, that is actively being exploited in the wild. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to bypass authentication due to insufficient authentication controls on an API endpoint.

top_stories.title: The Pillar Cracks Three Ways: Azure Identity Infrastructure Takes Three Max-Severity Hits in One Patch Tuesday
top_stories.summary: Microsoft's September 2026 Patch Tuesday addressed three maximum-severity vulnerabilities targeting the Azure identity infrastructure, part of a record-breaking 964 CVE patch cycle. All three flaws directly affect Azure's identity stack, posing significant risks to authentication and access management systems built on Microsoft's cloud platform.

top_stories.title: Microsoft Entra Agent ID Expands with MCP Firewall, Adding Network-Level Control to Agent Governance
top_stories.summary: Microsoft is expanding its Entra Agent ID governance framework with the introduction of an MCP Firewall, adding network-level control to AI agent management. The new capability provides security teams with additional controls to govern AI agents operating in enterprise production environments within the Microsoft Entra ecosystem.

top_stories.title: MFA Won't Save You From OAuth Consent Abuse
top_stories.summary: The article argues that MFA is insufficient to protect against OAuth consent abuse attacks, where attackers trick users into granting malicious applications access to their accounts. The piece highlights the need for OAuth governance controls including least-privilege scopes, consent monitoring, and token revocation capabilities as necessary complements to MFA.

news.title: Claude Opus 5 Helped Researchers Take Over OpenAI Staff Accounts via Chained Flaws
news.summary: Security researchers at Hacktron used Claude Opus 5 to chain two vulnerabilities—a bug in OpenAI's help forum software and a weakness in OpenAI's login system—to take over ChatGPT and Codex accounts of OpenAI employees and access an internal code repository. The attack exploited flaws in OpenAI's authentication and account management infrastructure, demonstrating AI-assisted account takeover via chained identity and login weaknesses.

news.title: Identity Visibility in 2026: The Foundation of Identity Security
news.summary: An article examines identity visibility as a foundational element of identity security in IAM, citing credential theft as a leading breach vector per Verizon's DBIR. The piece covers what identity visibility means in IAM contexts and how cloud and multicloud environments create additional complexity for managing it.

news.title: SolarWinds Patches ARM Hard-Coded Key Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated RCE
news.summary: SolarWinds has patched a high-severity vulnerability (CVE-2026-28326, CVSS 8.8) in its Access Rights Manager (ARM) product involving a hard-coded key that could allow unauthenticated remote code execution. The flaw affects all versions of Access Rights Manager 2026.2 and prior.

news.title: CrowdSec Says TanStack npm Attack Led to Copy of 170 Private GitHub Repositories
news.summary: CrowdSec disclosed that approximately 170 private GitHub repositories were copied by an attacker on May 22, exploiting the active account of a recently departed employee whose offboarding had not included revoking GitHub access. The breach originated from a supply chain attack on TanStack npm packages that stole credentials from the former employee's laptop, highlighting failures in access deprovisioning and identity lifecycle management.

news.title: Fake LastPass Authenticator GitHub repos push new Rapuncel infostealer
news.summary: A malware campaign is using SEO-optimized GitHub repositories to impersonate LastPass Authenticator and other software firms to distribute a new infostealer called Rapuncel. The campaign specifically targets authentication and password management tools, posing a direct threat to users seeking legitimate IAM-related software downloads.

news.title: Secure enterprise sharing with access reviews for Microsoft 365
news.summary: tenfold Software has published guidance on managing file-sharing access sprawl in Microsoft 365 through centralized access governance and owner-driven access reviews. The piece addresses how organizations can gain visibility into and remediate stale or unnecessary access permissions to sensitive data in Microsoft 365 environments.

news.title: Microsoft Patches CVSS 10.0 Azure AI Foundry Flaw Enabling Unauthorized Privilege Escalation
news.summary: Microsoft patched a maximum-severity (CVSS 10.0) vulnerability in Azure AI Foundry, tracked as CVE-2026-85889, that allowed unauthorized attackers to escalate privileges over a network. The flaw stemmed from missing authentication for a critical function, and Microsoft states no customer action is required as fixes have been deployed.

news.title: SailPoint’s (SAIL) Falcon Next-Gen SIEM Arrangement Fits Its Broader Identity Security Push
news.summary: SailPoint expanded its strategic alliance with CrowdStrike, integrating with CrowdStrike's Falcon Next-Gen SIEM platform. The partnership advances SailPoint's identity security capabilities by combining identity governance data with CrowdStrike's threat detection and security operations tooling.

news.title: Jim Cramer Says AI Could Make Okta’s Security Software More Essential
news.summary: Jim Cramer commented on Okta during a Mad Money episode, stating that AI is not making Okta's identity security software obsolete. The segment is a brief media mention of Okta framed around AI trends rather than reporting any concrete company news or product developments.

news.title: Why Shares of Okta Stock Shot Up 10% This Week
news.summary: Okta's stock rose 10% this week, driven by positive market momentum among cybersecurity names and solid earnings results. The article covers the financial performance of the identity and authentication platform vendor Okta.

news.title: jumpserver v5.0.0
news.summary: JumpServer has released version 5.0.0 of its open-source Privileged Access Management platform. The platform provides DevOps and IT teams with secure access to SSH, RDP, Kubernetes, Database, and RemoteApp endpoints through a web browser.

news.title: Gyazo Breach Exposes 23.62 Million User Records and 490 Million Image Metadata Records
news.summary: Gyazo, an image-sharing service operated by Helpfeel, suffered a data breach exposing approximately 23.62 million user records including email addresses and password hashes. The breach also exposed around 490 million image metadata records, primarily for images from January 2019 or earlier.

news.title: keycloak v26.7.4
news.summary: Keycloak has released version 26.7.4 of its open source identity and access management platform. The release continues support for modern applications and services through the open source IAM project maintained by Red Hat.

news.title: vault v2.1.1
news.summary: HashiCorp Vault version 2.1.1 has been released as a tool covering secrets management, encryption as a service, and privileged access management. No specific details about changes, fixes, or new features in this release are provided in the description.

news.title: Implementing defense-in-depth authorization for MCP tools on Amazon Quick
news.summary: The article provides a technical walkthrough for implementing defense-in-depth authorization for Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools on Amazon Bedrock using Microsoft Entra ID. The implementation uses Entra ID group and claims-based JWTs through an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway interceptor to enforce per-user, per-tool access controls.

news.title: Amplifier Extends Workforce Security to the AI Agents Employees Build and Use
news.summary: Amplifier Security announced Agent Intent & Posture Management (AIPM), a capability that connects discovered AI agents to employee owners and documents each agent's stated purpose for risk remediation. The product extends workforce security to AI agents built and used by employees, addressing identity and access governance concerns around non-human identities.

news.title: Druva expands identity resilience with ransomware detection
news.summary: Druva has announced new capabilities for its Identity Resilience product alongside a new Ransomware Detection feature powered by a proprietary AI threat pipeline called Dru MetaGraph. The additions use behavioral intelligence to enhance identity protection within Druva's data security platform.

news.title: EU Cyber Resilience Act to Enforce New Reporting Requirements
news.summary: The EU Cyber Resilience Act begins enforcing a 24-hour mandatory reporting requirement for serious product security incidents affecting European organizations. This regulation directly impacts IAM vendors and practitioners operating in the EU who must now report significant security vulnerabilities or incidents within this compressed timeframe.

news.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
news.summary: Microsoft released a record-breaking patch batch addressing at least 974 security vulnerabilities across Windows and other software. AI is being credited for accelerating vulnerability discovery, though security experts note organizations are struggling to keep pace with testing and deploying the volume of fixes.

news.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
news.summary: A dark web service is selling digital scans of over 153 million U.S. and Canadian drivers licenses, apparently sourced from a Louisiana-based identity verification company. The FBI's New Orleans field office has opened an official inquiry into the breach.

news.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
news.summary: Canadian cybercriminal Connor Riley Moucka pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy charges for hacking and extorting over 165 organizations using Snowflake's cloud data storage platform. The case involved credential-based attacks targeting Snowflake customer accounts, resulting in the theft of over 100 million AT&T customer records including call and text history.
